singleMonthReport.diagnosisAboveBenchmark: Diagnosis: this month is running above the directional benchmark; inspect the top fee drivers first.
singleMonthReport.diagnosisNearBenchmark: Diagnosis: this month is close to the directional benchmark; top fee drivers are still worth checking.
singleMonthReport.rateComparisonBody: Your card/charge processing rate is {chargeRate} ({rateGap}). Stripe's advertised card rate starts at 2.9% + $0.30, but the real rate often moves higher because of fixed fees, international cards, and card mix. Your all-in Stripe cost rate for this export is {allInRate}.
singleMonthReport.allInFeesSubtitle: Charge fees plus refunds, disputes, payouts & other Stripe fee lines

multiMonthReport.diagnosisAboveBenchmark: Diagnosis: your blended rate is materially above the directional benchmark; start with savings opportunities and high-fee charges.
multiMonthReport.diagnosisNearWithAnomalies: Diagnosis: your blended rate is close to baseline, but several transactions are still worth reviewing.
multiMonthReport.diagnosisConsistent: Diagnosis: your blended rate looks consistent; monitor monthly changes for future spikes.
multiMonthReport.rateComparisonBody: Your card/charge processing rate is {chargeRate} ({rateGap}). Stripe's advertised card rate starts at 2.9% + $0.30, but international cards, small charges, card mix, currency conversion, and add-ons can push the real rate higher. Your all-in Stripe cost rate for this export is {allInRate}{adjustedNote}.
multiMonthReport.anomalyPreviewLocked: {count} charges cleared above your statistical threshold vs your baseline — unlock for categories and line-by-line tips.
multiMonthReport.anomalyPaidGeneric: {count} charges paid above your ~{baseline}% baseline — common when card mix includes international or premium interchange; not necessarily errors.
multiMonthReport.anomalyPaidDetailed: {count} charges paid above your ~{baseline}% baseline.{sampleCopy} About {pct}% of {scope} are tagged "{label}". Typical when international or premium cards are a large share; not necessarily errors.
multiMonthReport.chargesAboveBaselineSubtitle: Charges with a higher fee rate than your typical mix — not necessarily errors
multiMonthReport.noHighFeeCharges: No high-fee charges detected. Your fee rate looks consistent!
multiMonthReport.markOneOffHint: Mark one-off charges (large refunds, international spikes) as expected so they do not skew your typical processing rate. Dollar totals stay unchanged.
multiMonthReport.unlockHighFeeHint: Unlock to see which charges are above your baseline and why
multiMonthReport.monthlyBreakdownLocked: Detailed monthly breakdown is in the paid report

lowVolumeReport.chargesAnalyzed: {count} charges analyzed — statistical high-fee detection requires 50+ transactions.
lowVolumeReport.diagnosisAboveBenchmark: Diagnosis: your small sample is above the directional benchmark; upload a longer range to confirm the pattern.
lowVolumeReport.diagnosisTooSmall: Diagnosis: this sample is too small for statistical high-fee detection; upload more months for a stronger read.
lowVolumeReport.rateComparisonBody: Your card/charge processing rate is {chargeRate} ({rateGap}). On low-volume exports, fixed $0.30 fees and a few high-fee charges can move the blended rate a lot. Your all-in Stripe cost rate for this export is {allInRate}.
lowVolumeReport.noteBody: High-fee charge detection and trend analysis require 50+ charge transactions. Export a longer date range (3–12 months) and re-analyze for full statistical insights.
lowVolumeReport.deeperAnalysisBody: Export a longer date range from Stripe to unlock high-fee charge detection and trend charts.

reportDashboardCharts.title: Where your Stripe fees concentrate
reportDashboardCharts.intlMoreExpensive: Intl is ~{pct}% more expensive per dollar · {share}% of volume · ~{fees} uplift estimate
reportDashboardCharts.radarFootnote: Axes = share of all-in fees by leak bucket (directional; some estimates can overlap).
reportDashboardCharts.timelineFootnote: Bar length = fee dollars that month (Gantt-style intensity). Label inside = processing rate.

feeLeakBreakdown.title: Fee dollars, translated into actions
feeLeakBreakdown.intro: Direct allocation comes from your Stripe Balance CSV. Estimated impact separates likely fixed-fee drag, international uplift, and refund effects — these may overlap, so do not add calculated and estimated buckets together as guaranteed savings.
feeLeakBreakdown.directSubtitle: Direct fee rows plus calculated allocation of charge fees. Evidence level is shown per bucket.
feeLeakBreakdown.directAdditiveNote: Direct rows from your CSV — these add up to {total} ({pct}% of all-in fees).
feeLeakBreakdown.estimatedSubtitle: Directional diagnostics for patterns Stripe does not always show as separate rows. Overlap is expected — do not sum with direct allocation.

reportReconciliation.title: How the report totals tie out
reportReconciliation.subtitle: Arithmetic check against uploaded Balance rows. This is not payout, bank, or general-ledger reconciliation.

savingsOpportunities.intro: Problem → potential cost in this export → what to inspect in Stripe. Annual figures are directional; scenarios can overlap — treat them as prioritization, not guaranteed savings.
savingsOpportunities.periodCost: ~{amount} potential cost in this export period
savingsOpportunities.achWarning: ACH can reduce card fees on large invoices, but bank transfers add checkout friction, failure/retry risk, and longer settlement. Best for B2B invoices where customers already pay by bank transfer — not a blanket swap for every card charge.

moneyFirstImpact.headlineDiagnosis: We found a concrete fee driver
moneyFirstImpact.diagnosisUnlock: {body} Unlock the full report to see every affected row, the caveats, and what to inspect first.
moneyFirstImpact.savingsBody: Your first directional opportunity appears to be {label}{confidence}. Unlock the full report to see the affected rows, caveats, and next actions.
moneyFirstImpact.rateGapBody: Your processing rate sits {label}. Unlock the full report to see which charges and fee drivers create that gap — and what to check in Stripe.
moneyFirstImpact.runrateBody: You're on track for ~{amount}/yr in Stripe fees at this rate. Unlock to see high-fee rows, drivers, and directional savings actions.
moneyFirstImpact.gatedHighFeeSingular: {count} high-fee charge cleared above your baseline. Unlock to see why and what to inspect.
moneyFirstImpact.gatedHighFeePlural: {count} high-fee charges cleared above your baseline. Unlock to see why and what to inspect.

moneyFirstImpact.disclaimer: Estimates are directional and calculated from this upload — not guaranteed savings.

reportTrustChecklist.title: Three numbers to match against Stripe
reportTrustChecklist.body: Before trusting any insight, compare these against the same Balance CSV date range in Stripe. The processing rate is simply charge fees divided by charge volume.

firstActionCallout.notGuaranteed: Not guaranteed savings · scenarios may overlap

internationalCardUplift.title: International cards are lifting your rate
internationalCardUplift.body: {count, plural, one {# international-looking charge paid} other {# international-looking charges paid}} above your domestic mix. That is about {amount} of directional cross-border/card-mix uplift in this export.
internationalCardUplift.disclaimer: Estimate compares visible international-looking charges with your domestic mix.

refundFeeLeakage.title: Refunds left processing fees behind
refundFeeLeakage.body: {count, plural, one {# refund left} other {# refunds left}} an estimated {amount} in retained processing fees in this export.
refundFeeLeakage.disclaimer: Stripe commonly does not return the original processing fee after a refund.

smallTicketDrag.title: Small charges are amplifying fixed fees
smallTicketDrag.body: {count, plural, one {# charge under $20 paid} other {# charges under $20 paid}} {rate} on average. Fixed per-charge fees account for about {amount} across this export.
smallTicketDrag.disclaimer: This is the fixed-fee component of your card charges, not a claim that it is avoidable.

otherFeeLines.title: Non-processing Stripe fee lines showed up
otherFeeLines.body: {amount} in non-charge Stripe fee lines appears in this export, separate from card processing fees.

aboveBenchmarkRate.title: Your processing rate is above this mix's benchmark
aboveBenchmarkRate.body: Your {chargeRate} processing rate is {rateGap} percentage points above the rough {expectedRate} benchmark for this mix — about {amount} across this export.
aboveBenchmarkRate.disclaimer: This is a directional benchmark, not proof that the difference is avoidable.

unusualCharge.title: One charge deserves a closer look
unusualCharge.body: We found an unusually high-fee charge with {amount} in Stripe fees. The full report explains the pattern and shows the affected rows.

internationalCardFees.tip: Cross-border cards can add ~{crossBorderPercent}% on top of standard domestic pricing. Local payment methods can reduce that in supported markets.
internationalCardFees.step1: Enable SEPA Direct Debit (EU) or iDEAL (Netherlands)
internationalCardFees.step2: Offer local methods at checkout for EU/UK customers

smallTransactions.tip: {count} charges under {currency} 20 (avg {currency} {avgAmount}). Bundling or monthly billing cuts repeated fixed fees.
smallTransactions.step1: Set a minimum charge in checkout where it fits your model
smallTransactions.step2: Move sub-$10 subs to one monthly invoice

achLargeInvoices.tip: {count} charges over $500 on cards. ACH is ~0.8% (max $5) vs card pricing. Annual figure uses a conservative switching share, not a full migration.
achLargeInvoices.periodLossNote: if every eligible invoice moved from card to ACH this period
achLargeInvoices.annualSavingsNote: if ~{share}% of eligible large invoices switch
achLargeInvoices.step1: Enable ACH Direct Debit under Payment methods

outlierRateComparison.spikeQuestion: Is the spike a recurring leak — or a one-off?
outlierRateComparison.adjustedHint: Mark high-fee charges as expected one-offs below. Adjusted rate shows your typical mix without those rows skewing the average.
outlierRateComparison.footnote: Dollar totals still include everything Stripe charged. Use this to separate recurring leaks (intl cards, refunds, small tickets) from one-off spikes.
outlierRateComparison.partialLedgerNote: Large exports adjust marked rows only — re-upload a shorter CSV for full-period recalc.

feeInsightCards.expectedRange: Rough expected range for this mix
feeInsightCards.expectedRangeNote: Directional estimate based on charge size, fixed fees, visible cross-border/non-USD patterns, and refunds.
feeInsightCards.refundBody: {count} refund totaling {volume}. Stripe generally keeps the original processing fee when you refund, so this is an estimated margin leak.
feeInsightCards.refundBodyPlural: {count} refunds totaling {volume}. Stripe generally keeps the original processing fee when you refund, so this is an estimated margin leak.
feeInsightCards.directRefundFees: Includes {amount} of direct refund-row fees found in the CSV.
feeInsightCards.noRefundBody: No refund rows were detected in this export. If refunds happen outside this date range, export a longer period to measure their fee impact.

geographyBreakdown.title: You pay {pct}% more on international charges
geographyBreakdown.summaryBody: International charges average {intlRate} vs {domRate} domestic — about {pctDiff}% more per dollar processed. They make up {intlShare}% of charge volume. The slice we attribute to international uplift (international fees minus what the same volume would cost at your domestic effective rate) is about {intlExcessShare}% of charge fees — so most absolute fee dollars still come from domestic volume, even though each international dollar is pricier.
geographyBreakdown.tipHighIntlShare: Switching EU customers to SEPA Direct Debit or iDEAL eliminates the 1.5% cross-border surcharge entirely.
geographyBreakdown.tipDefault: Enable local payment methods (SEPA, iDEAL) for international customers to reduce cross-border costs.

monitorHistory.title: Rate drift across your uploads
monitorHistory.subtitle: Private summary history linked to the subscriber email. Active Monitor reports are retained for up to 13 months.
monitorHistory.baselineMessage: This is your baseline report. Upload the next period with the same subscriber email to unlock month-over-month rate and fee deltas.
monitorHistory.deltaFootnote: Deltas compare whole uploaded periods. Use similar date ranges for a clean month-over-month comparison.

shareEmbedBenchmark.title: Show others what Stripe really costs you

shareEmbedBenchmark.inLine: — roughly in line with that midpoint.
shareEmbedBenchmark.midpointDisclaimer: Midpoints are modeled guesses for storytelling — not live market averages or Stripe-official stats.
shareEmbedBenchmark.twitterHint: X opens with text ready to post. Attach the PNG for extra reach — graphs outperform text-only posts.
shareEmbedBenchmark.embedBody: Paste as "Embed" or HTML block. Anyone with this iframe URL can see summary stats — keep your link private.

transactionBuckets.title: Fee Rate by Transaction Size
transactionBuckets.subtitle: Smaller transactions pay more due to the fixed $0.30 fee. All size tiers are listed; empty tiers show 0 charges.
transactionBuckets.smallTicketInsight: 💡 Your small transactions (<$20) have a {rate} effective rate — the fixed $0.30 fee is disproportionately large. Consider bundling or minimum charge limits.
